feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital leadership CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector experience. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across skills sections, and could use sharper outcome-focused achievements to increase impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear executive profile: the headline and summary quickly establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Credible experience progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement supports leadership credibility and domain depth.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would help (e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, campaign performance).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve structure and readability.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/subjective for education; punctuation and bullet formatting in the footer/projects section feel compressed and inconsistent. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It would be sharper with one concrete scale indicator and slightly less overlap with the competencies and experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing: change “more than 12 years of experience” to “12+ years’ experience” and simplify “behind high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add one proof point from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Reduce list density by grouping related areas: “web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations” rather than naming every function.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years’ experience modernizing web, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads enterprise Drupal platforms, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled discovery experiences, including a 10,000+ page migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations” and the long capability list repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent project and skills sections; “AI-enabled discovery experiences” is more specific.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad CV language.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- If space is tight, cut either “public-sector” or “advocacy” to avoid stacking adjacent concepts.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it shorter and more category-based than descriptive.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already well covered in work experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Strengthen specificity: e.g., “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “bill-level AI chat,” and “10×20-foot conference display” are good—add audience, scale, or purpose where possible.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed/Launched… to support/improve/expand…”
- Consider this tighter wording: “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search,” the microsite, and the video series closely repeat current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; prioritize similarly unique projects here.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a services list rather than a high-impact position. Tighten it around outcomes, platform scale, and 2–3 signature contributions that complement—not repeat—your NACo leadership role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards, and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make technical/platform work more concise and specific: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes wherever possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, time saved, search improvements, campaign performance, or reduction in troubleshooting/publishing friction.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep this version shorter unless you can show a new result.
- AI-enabled search also appears in Recent Projects; mention it briefly here and let the project section carry the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email engagement, audience growth, campaign performance, or production volume if available; “reaching tens of thousands” is vague.
- Condense into 4–5 bullets, e.g.: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video/programming language overlaps with the footer projects and prior NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more role-specific by emphasizing operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the larger-scale leadership achievements in the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on executional leadership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy content across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scope: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” are vague and partially duplicate governance/operations language in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership themes and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and content strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Editorial planning and content operations.”
- Make the list more distinct from Core Competencies by focusing on leadership scope, not channel coverage.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications operations
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Editorial planning and audience strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is close to both the header and Core Competencies; consider “Cross-channel communications operations” to reduce repetition.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the most current, differentiating strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-platform mentions here unless central to current targeting; move “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery” to Technical + IT only.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer impact language, e.g. “Web platforms, integrations & automation” or “CMS platforms & digital implementation.”
- If space allows, tie to scale/value: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “platforms supporting high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost line-for-line.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” and “workflow automation” already appear in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or remove one instance.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” technical list. Tighten this item to emphasize strategic analytics leadership rather than repeating tool names alone.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the highest-value, recent strengths first: KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, analytics strategy, then tools.
- Use “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to outcomes from recent roles: analytics infrastructure for a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; consider making Topline Skills more strategic and leaving full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless supported by a concrete optimization example elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more leadership- and outcomes-oriented, reflecting recent studio/event work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-value bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add one impact cue in the section intro or elsewhere: e.g., “Built NACo’s first in-house video studio to expand advocacy and event production capacity.”
- Use “post-production” instead of “editing” and “multi-camera production workflows” instead of just “PTZ camera systems” for stronger phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- Specific tools belong in Technical + IT, so keep this section focused on capability areas, not equipment/tool lists.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to sharpen relevance around recent CMS leadership and reduce duplication.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platform Administration**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: **Drupal** first, then the others in descending relevance.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful production use; it reads lighter than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills item [2]; either merge them or make this version more implementation-focused while Topline stays strategic.
- Avoid repeating generic platform names elsewhere without context; Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so the value here is specificity, not repetition.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding terms to applied execution: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome language elsewhere in the CV tied to these tools, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics/tag deployment, and workflow automation.”
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”); avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Topline Skills, so keep GitHub Actions framed specifically as deployment/CI.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list. It would be stronger if grouped by function and framed around systems you actually used to improve coordination and automation in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add light impact context instead of a pure list, e.g.: “Used to build editorial planning systems, automate handoffs/notifications, and support cross-team communications workflows.”
- Keep only the most relevant/current platforms; consider dropping older or lighter-use tools to avoid looking tool-stuffed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack and Teams are generic collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize automation/project systems over basic comms platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership, but this line is too bare and doesn’t reflect level of use or strategic ownership. It would be stronger if framed as campaign/email platforms rather than just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Keep the list concise and current: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add level/context instead of more tools: Enterprise email campaigns, member communications, and audience journeys
- If these platforms were central in recent roles, consider: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter operations • Audience segmentation

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters” or channel leadership language already covered in recent NACo roles.
- Don’t add analytics or automation terms here; those are already covered in separate Technical + IT categories.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for the recent NACo leadership work, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should read more like a focused tools list and avoid repeating broader capability terms.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad nouns with more specific skill framing: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting”
- Consider dropping either “Dashboarding” or “Looker Studio/Power BI”; the tools already imply dashboard creation.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to impact in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built reporting infrastructure” or “improved decision-making.”
- Keep the order weighted to recent, higher-value analytics platforms: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep one version broader and this one strictly tool-based.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are capabilities, not tools; they may fit better in competencies than Technical + IT.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong foundation, but this reads broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and “early-build” oriented, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale markers if you have them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around progression and team-building: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Emphasize hands-on execution over leadership language used later: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video production, cross-channel publishing workflows.
- Tighten phrasing and remove filler: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and recurring weekly video updates, and improved cross-channel publishing workflows. Provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if possible, distinguish this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or save workflow/governance emphasis for later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support plus the notable “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout accomplishment: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more active, e.g. “produced digital and multimedia content to support program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.
- Consider a two-part structure: 1) innovation/research coordination, 2) podcast/digital content launch.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership here; later positions better establish progression into management.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item reads more like a mixed capability list than a clean tools section. It should be tightened and aligned to recent senior multimedia work, while avoiding overlap with broader “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or narrow to emphasize software/tools: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep workflows, separate tools from capabilities: “Adobe Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator; livestream studio operations; podcast production”
- Use consistent specificity: prefer “Adobe Premiere Pro” over “Premiere Pro,” and consider dropping “Photoshop/Illustrator” if they are only occasional tools
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., studio buildout, recurring video series, podcast launch)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Livestreaming • PTZ camera systems • Studio operations • Hybrid and virtual event production”
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older NACo experience; keep it only if still relevant to current target roles
